verdict.rationale: Groq's own Batch API lets users submit thousands of API requests as one asynchronous batch, at 50% lower cost and without affecting standard rate limits. This directly delivers bulk processing across many items. It comes with documented limits: a 24-hour to 7-day processing window, and availability only after upgrading to a paid plan. Missing for 10: documentation of how a batch is built and managed (input file format, status monitoring, cancellation, result retrieval), synchronous or near-real-time bulk options, and independent or hands-on corroboration of batch usage.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can perform bulk operations across many items at once

citations.quote: Batch processing lets you run thousands of API requests at scale by submitting your workload as an asynchronous batch of requests to Groq with 50% lower cost, no impact to your standard rate limits, and 24-hour to 7 day processing window.
Process large-scale workloads asynchronously with our Batch API
Immediately after upgrading, you unlock several benefits: Higher Token Limits... Flex Service Tier... Batch Processing... Spend Limits
